title: Map Editors for Three.js & Blender?
author: Lola_Montezz
selftext:
Hi fellow builders,

I'm about to start a new project and I'd like to hear your experiences on what worked well for you for AI game development. I'm planning to make a browser-based idle-ish game that has some small-ish maps where players. Think something like Brighter Shores (though simpler graphics, less animation-heavy, more idle-like, but the concept of relatively small traversable maps, isometric-ish).

The idea is to leverage Three.js because of the framework maturity and extensive Javascript  training data. I'm planning to use Blender MCP, because I personally suck at art, so I plan to let Claude use create basic 3D models for my game. My starting point is to pick an art style, texture style, character skeleton style, etc. and create an extensive design language to have it generate more consistent style art.

I've built 2D games (and engines) myself in the past pre-AI, but never 3D. I've worked with game/rendering engines that mostly used Ortographic cameras on 2D pixel art, using Tiled. I'd like to hear your experiences working with Blender MCP (what worked well for you guys to get consistent output), your experiences working with Three.js + Blender, and finally the main topic I'm interested in now: **What map editor do you use to create 3D levels that supports Blender objects, but also allows things like map properties (entity spawns, item locations, world objects, etc.) that work well with Three.js? Bonus if Claude can put objects in the editor as well :)**

Thanks for reading :)

comments.author: Zenpher
comments.body:
try playcanvas instead, you'll get better out of the box performance and entity/object support

threejs is actually pretty terrible as a game engine

replies.author: Lola_Montezz
replies.body:
I'll take a look, thanks for the recommendation. I picked Three.js for two reasons: It's been out for ages, so LLMs are heavily trained on it (as well as JS/TS in general), plus it runs in the browser, so I can use something like playwright-cli to automate e2e tests for my game or even let Claude prove features work by playing them. 

What didn't you like about Three.js? I've started working with it now, with Blender MCP and it works pretty well so far for me when you invest a bit upfront in your local agent setup and instructions/skills. I have a Blender scene rendered with some basic terrain mesh and humanoid figure that can walk around the mesh.

replies.author: Zenpher
replies.body:
The performance was kind of bad and I ended up having to implement a ton of the lighting, collision, etc..

I'm working on a large project right now and when I switched from threejs to playcanvas I gained 50-70% performance basically for free. The main issue was inefficient CPU usage which was proving very difficult to optimize for in threejs.

This is my project btw  [https://apsis.formandelement.com/](https://apsis.formandelement.com/)

replies.author: Lola_Montezz
replies.body: Thanks for sharing that. That's a very big map indeed! My use case would likely be a ton smaller with instanced relatively small maps, so I reckon it should be more managable. Did you run into CPU issues due to JS being inherently single threaded?

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: Ask Claude to cook up an editor based on your game then.
